references.text: Proverbs encourages finishing the work outdoors and having everything ready before building a house – a parallel to Jesus' teaching on planning fully before beginning construction ([ref:Prov 24:27|Proverbs 24:27]).
Joshua asks the people to go through the land and describe it before taking possession of it, an image of necessary planning before action ([ref:Josh 18:4|Joshua 18:4]).

The preceding verse sets the context: Jesus says one must first sit down and calculate the cost before beginning to build a tower, leading to the warning in verse 29 about the consequences of failing to do so ([ref:Luke 14:28|Luke 14:28]).
The following verse completes the parable: people will say that this man began to build but was not able to finish – the result of lack of planning ([ref:Luke 14:30|Luke 14:30]).

Paul urges the Corinthians to complete what they have started, not only having good intentions but also following through – a parallel to the warning about being able to finish what one begins ([ref:2 Cor 8:10-11|2 Corinthians 8:10-11]).
Hebrews encourages moving forward from the foundation that has been laid and reaching maturity, using the same building metaphor of laying a foundation (θεμέλιον) ([ref:Heb 6:1|Hebrews 6:1]).
Paul expresses confidence that God will complete the good work He has begun – a contrast to the man in the parable who was unable to finish ([ref:Phil 1:6|Philippians 1:6]).

A warning about unfinished projects: one should build a house but not live in it – an image of started but incomplete work, paralleling the unfinished building in Jesus' parable ([ref:Deut 28:30|Deuteronomy 28:30]).
